title: Exact equivalences of thick subcategories transport ambient thick closures
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be triangulated categories [def-weil-triangulated-category], let $\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal B\subseteq\mathcal D$ be full thick subcategories [pur9-def-thick] with the induced triangulated structures, and let $E:\mathcal A\simeq\mathcal B$ be an equivalence whose forward and inverse functors are exact. For any class $\mathscr S$ of objects of $\mathcal A$, write $\langle\mathscr S\rangle_{\mathcal C}$ for the smallest full subcategory of $\mathcal C$ containing $\mathscr S$ and zero and closed under isomorphisms, integer shifts, distinguished cones and retracts, and define $\langle E\mathscr S\rangle_{\mathcal D}$ in the same way. Then these closures lie in $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$, respectively, and for every object $K$ of $\mathcal A$ one has
$$K\in\langle\mathscr S\rangle_{\mathcal C}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad E(K)\in\langle E\mathscr S\rangle_{\mathcal D}.$$
Thus $E$ restricts to an equivalence between these ambient thick closures. The class $\mathscr S$ may be empty, and the ambient categories need not be idempotent complete.

proof.text: Let $H_{\mathcal C}=\langle\mathscr S\rangle_{\mathcal C}$. Since $\mathcal A$ is a full thick subcategory of $\mathcal C$ and contains $\mathscr S$, it is one of the thick subcategories occurring in the intersection that defines $H_{\mathcal C}$; hence every object of $H_{\mathcal C}$ lies in $\mathcal A$. The identical argument with $\mathcal B\subseteq\mathcal D$ shows that $H_{\mathcal D}=\langle E\mathscr S\rangle_{\mathcal D}$ lies in $\mathcal B$.

source.place: Unit proof, first paragraph: ambient thick-closure comparison (agent-supplied expansion)

proof.text: Compute the closure of $\mathscr S$ inside $\mathcal A$. The subcategory $H_{\mathcal C}$, regarded as a full subcategory of $\mathcal A$, is thick there: its closure operations are inherited from $\mathcal C$, and triangles in the induced structure are ambient distinguished triangles. Hence $\langle\mathscr S\rangle_{\mathcal A}\subseteq H_{\mathcal C}$. Conversely, $\langle\mathscr S\rangle_{\mathcal A}$ is thick in $\mathcal C$. It contains the ambient zero up to isomorphism, and ambient shifts are the induced shifts. Given an ambient distinguished triangle with two vertices in it, thickness of $\mathcal A$ puts the third in $\mathcal A$; fullness and the induced structure make that triangle a distinguished $\mathcal A$-triangle, so its third vertex lies in the relative closure. An ambient retract of one of its objects first lies in $\mathcal A$ by thickness of $\mathcal A$, and fullness puts the inclusion and retraction in $\mathcal A$, where relative retract closure applies. An ambient isomorphism is handled in the same way using isomorphism closure of $\mathcal A$ and fullness. Thus minimality in $\mathcal C$ gives the reverse inclusion. We obtain $H_{\mathcal C}=\langle\mathscr S\rangle_{\mathcal A}$ and, by this same argument for $\mathcal B\subseteq\mathcal D$, $H_{\mathcal D}=\langle E\mathscr S\rangle_{\mathcal B}$.

source.place: Unit proof, first paragraph: ambient thick-closure comparison (agent-supplied expansion)

proof.text: Write $H_{\mathcal A}=\langle\mathscr S\rangle_{\mathcal A}$, $H_{\mathcal B}=\langle E\mathscr S\rangle_{\mathcal B}$, and $G$ for the given exact inverse. Let $P$ be the full subcategory of $\mathcal A$ defined by $E(K)\in H_{\mathcal B}$. It is thick: additivity sends zero to zero, the shift comparisons send integer shifts to isomorphic shifts, and exactness sends a distinguished triangle to a distinguished triangle, so two vertices in $P$ force the third into $P$. A retract $K\xrightarrow{i}L\xrightarrow{r}K$ with $ri=1_K$ maps to $E(r)E(i)=1_{E(K)}$; hence $P$ is retract closed. Functors preserve isomorphisms, so $P$ is also isomorphism closed. Every $S\in\mathscr S$ belongs to $P$. The intersection definition therefore gives $H_{\mathcal A}\subseteq P$, proving $K\in H_{\mathcal A}\Rightarrow E(K)\in H_{\mathcal B}$. Now define $Q\subseteq\mathcal B$ by $G(L)\in H_{\mathcal A}$. The same operation-by-operation check with the given exact functor $G$ makes $Q$ thick. It contains every $E(S)$ because the equivalence unit gives $GE(S)\cong S\in H_{\mathcal A}$. Thus $H_{\mathcal B}\subseteq Q$. If $E(K)\in H_{\mathcal B}$, this gives $GE(K)\in H_{\mathcal A}$, and the unit isomorphism $GE(K)\cong K$ proves $K\in H_{\mathcal A}$.

source.place: Unit proof, first paragraph: ambient thick-closure comparison (agent-supplied expansion)

proof.text: Step 2 identifies the relative closures with the ambient closures, and Step 3 proves $K\in H_{\mathcal A}\Longleftrightarrow E(K)\in H_{\mathcal B}$ for each $K\in\mathcal A$. Hence $E$ restricts to the two ambient closures. The inclusion $H_{\mathcal B}\subseteq Q$ in Step 3 lets $G$ restrict in the other direction; fullness lets the original unit and counit restrict as well, giving the required equivalence. With $\mathscr S$ empty, the same intersection and inverse-image arguments apply without choosing a generator. At no point is an idempotent split: only already existing retract equations are mapped by the functors, so no idempotent-completeness hypothesis is used.
